attributional_sentence: The electricity term is an attributional footprint: annual electricity consumption multiplied by a generation-side average carbon intensity for the state. It answers what share of the state's average generation emissions goes with this load, not what emissions would be induced by adding it; the consequential question requires a long-run marginal emission rate, which is reported separately and never inside one interval with the attributional central.

enforceable_standard.name: the enforceable-standard reading
enforceable_standard.what_it_is: the registered bound in which a clean-electricity floor is applied only where a statute is enforceable against a retail seller. It is not retired, it is delivered in full, and neither reading may be quoted without naming which one it is.

policy_vintage.name: the published Counterfactual Baseline case
policy_vintage.what_it_is: a policy-vintage bound -- what such a state would look like if the repealed federal light-duty tailpipe greenhouse-gas standard for model year 2027 and later were still in force (repealed effective 2026-04-20, 91 FR 7686). It is never called current federal policy.
policy_vintage.why_inherited: the v3.3 build's bounds directory is empty: the Counterfactual Baseline case is not rebuilt on the asymptotic continuation, and four rows of the number table that quote it read INHERITED_NOT_RE_MEASURED for the same reason. The interval carries the case beside it as a named line computed by its own harness.

grid.source: a published national grid projection (NREL Cambium 2024, mid case), balancing-area annual values rolled up to each state and rebased on the state's own registered starting clean share
grid.statutory_floor_rule: every enacted statutory clean-electricity target a state expresses as a share of retail sales or of generation is honoured as a floor at its own stated level and in its own stated year; capacity targets, peak-demand targets, reductions measured against a baseline, executive orders, utility board resolutions and repealed statutes are not honoured

interval.boundary: Author-model conditional interval: registered evidence-bounded parameter distributions, the fuel-to-direct-current conversion coefficient drawn triangular on its declared list, a registered prior on the statutory compliance level with an atom at the statutory value of one, one registered electricity scenario at equal weight and one registered survival shape at equal weight, propagated through the author's load model. Not a frequentist prediction interval.

deployment_scale_named_lines.the_model_is_exactly_linear_in_this_scal: every entry starts from a deployed stock of exactly zero, so each year's deployed stock is the declared scale times a fixed path, every load is that stock times a per-unit quantity, and a carbon intensity does not depend on the scale at all.  Each named line is therefore the central rescaled by the level over 0.30.  The equality is not assumed: the harness is RUN at the declared level and compared with the central rescaled, cell by cell, in gates.named_lines

interval.energy_interval_disclaimer: The electricity-scenario axis changes the carbon content of a kilowatt hour, not the number of kilowatt hours.  Its contribution to the energy interval is therefore exactly zero, and an energy figure must not be captioned as though the electricity axis were inside it.  The same holds for the post-2050 continuation rule ON THAT AXIS and for the reading of the statutory floor: the delivered central, the two electricity-axis continuation lines and the enforceable-standard line carry the same energy in every entry and in every year, bitwise, and they part company only in carbon.  The two VEHICLE-axis continuation lines are a different object and are not covered by this sentence: a rule on that axis moves how much of the deployed stock is electric, so it moves the kilowatt hours as well as the carbon, and the movement is reported rather than gated.

interval.not_priced_sentence: Not priced by this interval: the deployment scale, held at 30 per cent of registered automobiles and 30 per cent of signalized intersections by 2075 in every draw, against its own declared range of 15 to 45 per cent -- the model is exactly linear in that scale, so the two declared levels are delivered beside the interval as named lines, each of them the central rescaled, and never as width; the reading of the statutory floor itself, held at the statutory-targets-honoured reading in every draw, with the enforceable-standard reading delivered beside the interval as a named line rather than as width; the vehicle load model, held at the inherited one, with the single paired dynamometer measurement in the build's own precedent table delivered beside the interval as a named measured-load line; the computing workload growth of 2 per cent a year and the hardware efficiency floor of 0.25, neither of which is drawn or varied anywhere in this build; and the published market case, held at the policy state the interval is conditional on and carried as a named line.  The post-2050 continuation rule IS inside this interval: every electricity member continues along its own 2045-2050 slope at a decreasing rate after 2050 with the enacted statutory floors applied on top, and the linear trend and frozen continuations are delivered beside the interval as named lines.  The fuel-to-direct-current conversion coefficient IS priced here: it is drawn triangular on the declared list, support 0.17 to 0.2744 with its mode at the delivered central 0.21, so the two registered branches are the endpoints of the support this interval samples rather than values outside it, and each of them is also delivered as a named line.
interval.what_this_interval_does_not_produce: Turning points.  This product is a distribution over annual quantities on one policy state; the entry-level turning-point count is a property of the CENTRAL and is carried in the central's own products.  On the asymptotic continuation this interval is reported against, the census by 2075 reads 9 of 51, 8 states and the District of Columbia, which is two numbers because the District of Columbia is not a state.  The four-row disclosure that must travel with any such count is delivered in full beside this field, and so is the qualifier that names the entries whose count rests on an authored extension.  Nothing in this interval bears on any of those counts.
interval.width_quotation_rule: Width is quoted relative to the same-year central value, as half of the 5th-95th percentile interval over that central, and it is reported as the MEDIAN across the 51 entries. On each entry's real deployment scale the median relative half-width is 23.733640 % for energy consumption in 2050 and 23.119377 % in 2075, and 24.502042 % for direct CO2 emissions in 2050 and 24.348288 % in 2075. No entry's central direct CO2 is exactly zero at either year, so no entry is excluded from either median and the v3.1c exclusion of six entries has no successor. There is no quotable window and no year past which a width may not be quoted.

post_2050_continuation.formula: x(t) = 1 - (1 - x(2050)) * exp(-k (t - 2050)), with k = s(2050) / (1 - x(2050)) and s(2050) the axis's own published terminal slope
post_2050_continuation.sentence: After 2050 each published series continues along its own 2045-2050 slope at a decreasing rate, approaching but never reaching 100 per cent, and the enacted statutory floors still apply.

r3_disclosure.r4_qualifier: A turning count must travel with this qualifier.  Colorado is in the central census; New Mexico is in the central census.  Each of them rests on an authored extension of the vehicle schedule past model year 2032: their rule reaches 0.82 of new vehicles in 2032 and the schedule beyond that year is the build own, not the regulation own.

role: THE DELIVERED CENTRAL: the published Alternative Transportation case, with each entry's own vehicle rule applied as a floor over that projection, every enacted statutory clean-electricity target expressed as a share honoured as a floor at its own stated level and in its own stated year, and both axes continued after 2050 along their own published terminal slope at a decreasing rate.
